Department: Imaging | Institution: Amsterdam UMC (AMC) | Date: 15 Jan 2025 | Study: Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate

Indication: Follow-up for PSA 70.0 alongside a previously positive biopsy.

FINDINGS:
The gland measures 105.0 mL. A well-circumscribed hypointense focus occupies the right posterior peripheral zone at the base-to-mid level, spanning roughly 28 mm. Diffusion-weighted sequences show pronounced restriction, mirrored by corresponding ADC hypointensity. Contrast kinetics demonstrate prompt, localized enhancement against background parenchyma. Capsular integrity remains intact with no seminal vesicle involvement. Pelvic nodes appear normal. Skeletal survey reveals no metastatic deposits.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right posterior peripheral zone, base/mid, measuring ~28 mm.
PSAD 0.67 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.8852009.

previous_notes.text: General practitioner Dr. C. Peters logged a steady PSA climb on 12 Feb 2024, recording 30.1 ng/mL back in October 2022, 41.3 ng/mL by July 2023, and 55.6 ng/mL during May 2024. After conducting a fresh digital assessment and examining earlier biopsy outcomes, the individual was officially forwarded to the urology outpatient department for thorough reassessment and subsequent diagnostic steps.
